title: Fractions
objectives: Understand fractions as parts of a whole
Add and subtract fractions with like denominators
Convert between improper fractions and mixed numbers

introduction.context: Fractions represent parts of wholes and are everywhere in daily life - from cooking measurements (1/2 cup) to time (1/4 hour) to sharing pizza slices. Understanding fractions is crucial for advanced math.
introduction.connection: Fractions build on division from Chapter 4. A fraction like 3/4 means 3 ÷ 4, or 3 parts out of 4 equal parts.

concepts.title: Understanding Fractions
concepts.content: A fraction has two parts: the numerator (top) shows how many parts we have, and the denominator (bottom) shows how many equal parts make the whole.

concepts.title: Equivalent Fractions
concepts.content: Different fractions can represent the same amount. We can multiply or divide both numerator and denominator by the same number to create equivalent fractions.

steps: Since denominators are the same, add the numerators
commonErrors: Forgetting to simplify the final answer

hints: Think about what fraction means the same as 1/2
1/2 means 1 part out of 2 equal parts
practice.explanation: 2/4 = 1/2 because both represent half of a whole. 2 out of 4 parts is the same as 1 out of 2 parts.
When denominators are the same, add the numerators: 2 + 1 = 3, so 2/5 + 1/5 = 3/5
